chapter: Handy's Louisiana Shakers and Pelican Garden
title: Forming his own band for the Pelican Garden
summary: He formed his ten-piece Louisiana Shakers when the Pelican manager offered nights, and names the men.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: The first band I really joined playing saxophone was my own band. Handis, Louisiana, Shakers.
How did you get that band together? How did you get that band together?

Well, that's kind of a mystery. Let me see, I was playing up at Seven and Howard. And it's, uh, Smiley and Joe. Now, I can't think of his trumpet player's name. But he's out in California. I don't know. Anyway, that's where I was playing. Ridgely's brother was managing the Pelican Garden. And he was in there one night. And he heard me playing. And he called me off to stand. I went to his table. We had a couple of drinks. And he asked me, he said, Andy, why don't you get up a band and come play for me? I said, play for you. I said, where you got to play? He said, I manage the Pelican. I said, oh yeah? He said, yeah. He said, I can give you three full nights a month. Two of them, I said, well, what kind of band do you want there? He said, well, we only use big bands there. Eight to ten pieces of it. So, I told him I'd see him in a couple of days. Well, I did. I went and seen him. And, uh, I went and talked to several fellas and got them together. Told him the proponents of it. And, um, I went and bought the music. No, just, you know, just copies of orchestrations. I bought about ten or fifteen of them. And we met at the Pelican and went up there and locked the doors and we started wrestling with that music. And we got it down pretty good. What year was that? I was around thirty-two. And then, uh, we played there. From there I went to, uh, Bugalooza's, oh, numerous of times I played in Bugalooza's, a big band, at that big club there.
How many pieces you said it was?

Well, I had, uh, one time I had, uh, Alvin Alcorn on trumpet. Was that in the beginning, I mean, when you first formed? Yes. Yeah? I had, uh, Willie Pardew on second trumpet. And I had, uh, Lee Collins on third trumpet. I had, uh, Raymond Brown on trombone. Uh-huh. I had David Jones on tenor sax. I was playing fourth, I was playing fourth, Alton, Bodley on third, Alton. Who was that? Bodley. Bodley? Yeah. I don't remember him. Well, him and H.E. was raised up together. Was that his first name or second name? No, that was his, I think that was his last name. Uh-huh. I had H.E. on guitar. Old Man Kimball on bass, tuba. Uh-huh. Raymond, uh, what's Raymond's name? Brown. Piano player. Doris. Raymond Doris on, uh, on piano. Uh-huh. And who did you head on drums? Roy E.
